newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition stays united on revaluation plan.
newsitem.headline: German coalition stays united on revaluation plan.

text.p: German Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said on Monday after a four-hour crisis meeting with coalition leaders that the government remained "unified" on its plans to revalue Bundesbank assets this year.
Bohl told journalists outside the chancellery that there would be a debate on the asset revaluation plans of Finance Minister Theo Waigel in parliament on Wednesday morning.

"On the question of the revalution...we are still unified in our belief that this is right," Bohl said. Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) and the centrist Free Democrats (FDP) said last week they planned to revalue the Bundesbank's gold and currency assets despite central bank objections.

Bohl said the coalition was still at odds over plans to fill budget holes, but that they were making progress. He said that there still could be problems balancing the 1997 budget even if the coalition can raise funds through an accelerated privatisation of assets.

The FDP has ruled out tax increases to fill the holes while media reports say Waigel wants to plug a 15 billion mark ($8.8 billion) deficit with petrol tax increases or a delay in the cut in the so-called solidarity tax for the reconstruction of eastern Germany.

Bohl said that Waigel, who will state the government's position on the controversial asset revaluation plan in parliament on Wednesday, would also discuss the proposed law on revaluation with the Bundesbank during the coming days. ($ = 1.705 German Marks)
